desc: Ideate DP shape and pitfalls: parity of next pick, non-empty constraint, snapshot per item, zero/one behavior, product cap, and reachable-sum bounds.

Implement the prefix DP: compute sum bound/offset and early `-1` for unreachable `k`; maintain `dp[parity][product] = bitset of alternating sums` for non-empty subsequences only; snapshot per item, singleton starts, OVER sentinel for overflow-then-zero recovery.
Finalize answer by scanning both parity states at alternating sum `k`, returning the max achievable product or `-1` if none.

Write brute-force enumerator and differential test harness covering examples, edge cases (all-zeros, k=0 empty-subsequence trap, limit=1, parity-toggling ones, negative/unreachable k, overflow-then-zero), exhaustive small sweep, and randomized tests.
Hand-trace prime suspects (OVER-sentinel merging, singleton-start parity, shift bounds) against brute-force results on adversarial cases — all traced correctly.

Verify solution end-to-end: no code-execution environment available, so confirmed via complete inductive correctness argument, shift-bound safety proof, OVER-sentinel soundness proof, and hand-traces of all three examples plus every identified hazard case; performance bounded by ~800 live (parity, product) entries × 150 elements of C-level big-int ops, well within limits.
